title: Known word keys (264,828 words and K1-K3 phrases at every phase: repeating, sliding, progressive) and 45,104 sculpture readings as running keys, on one fully hidden alphabet: numeric key, true Quagmire III, true Quagmire II, hidden alphabet on one side
k4_result: 295,227,813 settings, 0 survivors: no setting has a solution of the 24 clue equations mod 26 with the letters in different places. 15.75M linear systems had to be solved exactly; the rest fell to the forced-equal key letters (S->S at 33 with K->K at 74, R->P at 28 and 66) or to the fixed dot products of the numeric models. Nothing was left to decrypt, and 0 settings were undecided.
controls: 3 shuffled K4s, each on a different third of the words (88,276 each) and all sculpture readings, about 137.3M settings each: 0 survivors in all three. Undecided (true Quagmire II with a running key, too few equations to list the solutions): 13, 1 and 20 settings; K4 had 0. Same picture as K4.
scope_limits: ONE hidden alphabet only; two different hidden alphabets (Quagmire IV) are not decidable this way. Keys only from the lists: 264,828 words and phrases of 2-26 letters (theme words, 22k common words, /usr/share/dict, every 4-26 letter window of the K1-K3 plaintexts) and attack 58's 224 distinct sculpture readings (both panels, K1-K3 plaintext grids, Morse; every d-th letter, d = 1-60; 2,334,946 offsets) as non-repeating running keys. No two-word combinations of dictionary words, no German, no misspelt keys beyond those in the lists. Sliding = running sum of the word; progressive = one step per pass (numeric key: +1 or -1 only; Quagmire III: any step). Sliding and progressive keys were not run on Quagmire II, and sculpture readings were only used as plain running keys. Quagmire II with a key added instead of subtracted (non-standard) not run. The clue positions are taken as exact. The planted Quagmire III running key was found but its 69 forced letters read only -5.37 on the big model, so for running keys the proof rests on the exact equations, not on reading.

negative.family: Word key on a hidden tableau
negative.hypothesis: K4 uses one hidden (non-keyword, arbitrary) alphabet with a key that is a real word, a K1-K3 phrase or a reading of the sculpture, at any key length including the lengths the unknown-key tests could not decide (13, 16, 18-24, 26+).
negative.scope: 264,828 words and K1-K3 phrase windows (2-26 letters) at every phase as repeating, sliding (running sum) and progressive keys, plus 45,104 sculpture reading streams (2.33M offsets) as running keys; models: one hidden alphabet both sides with the key valued on A-Z or KRYPTOS (C = P + k, C = k - P, any constant), true Quagmire III with the key letter located on the hidden alphabet (C = P + K, P - K, K - P; sliding with free start, progressive with any step), true Quagmire II (plain on A-Z or KRYPTOS), hidden plain or hidden cipher alphabet against A-Z or KRYPTOS; exact solution mod 26 requiring distinct letter positions; 295,227,813 settings.
negative.outcome: Dead in scope: 0 of 295.2M settings have any solution with distinct positions (3 shuffled K4s, 137.3M settings each: 0 survivors, 1-20 undecided Quagmire II running keys each; planted 9/9 with the alphabet recovered and 69-95 of 97 letters read).

follow_ups: Two-word keys on a hidden alphabet without listing word pairs: in true Quagmire III, C = P + K, the forced-equal key letters (positions 33 and 74 the same letter, 28 and 66 the same letter) and about 60 forced-different pairs are conditions on the key alone. For a key of length L made of word A then word B, each condition touches one or two letters, so words can be indexed by the letters they put at the few slots involved and joined by hash, as in attack 63. Count first how many (L, split) pairs leave fewer than about 1e6 joined candidates, then solve those exactly with kryptos/idea93_hidden.py.

The same known-key test with a hidden alphabet AND one simple transposition of the ciphertext (K3-style route or columnar widths 2-12): the forced-equal key letters move with the transposition, but the test stays about 50 microseconds per setting, so roughly 1e4 transpositions x the 20k most likely keys is affordable.

Quagmire II with a sculpture reading as running key is the one corner this run could not always decide (1-20 undecided settings per shuffled text, 0 for K4). An English-scored completion over the free alphabet positions (the 5 free dimensions mod 13) would close it; planted test: a running key from the cipher panel read by columns.
